justification: Contributes parallel context compaction (summarization of accumulated history) and characterizes it in the lab against a sequential baseline on HotpotQA and LoCoMo; no deployed use.

Contributes a runtime execution model that permits an action only if authority is constructible (admit/deny/halt gate); argued with an execution protocol and safety/liveness claims, no empirical study.
Contribution is the arrangement of peer agents around a shared reasoning hub and what they exchange, trained and then measured against strong baselines on long-horizon settings in the lab.
Contributes Belief Entropy plus MMPO to supervise the recursive-summary memory policy (what carries across steps); evaluated in the lab on long-horizon task suites up to 1.75M-token contexts.

PASTE changes what the loop does next by speculatively scheduling predicted tool calls alongside generation and confirming them later; measured on deep-research, coding and scientific-agent workloads.
Memex governs what state carries across steps: indexed experience memory with learned write/read/dereference policy; validated in the lab on long-horizon tasks plus a theoretical analysis.
AdaCoM trains an external manager that edits a frozen agent's context (prune stale, preserve constraints); lab evaluation across agents on web-search and deep-research benchmarks.

Novelty is the judge that validates a candidate compaction summary against the agent's continued reasoning before it is adopted, i.e. an acceptance check; measured on SWE-bench Verified and BrowseComp.
SkillSentry wraps the execution loop to monitor skill execution against DSL guidance and catch deviations; evaluated in the lab over 15 skills crossed with two agents and two backbone models.
Contribution is an MCTS variant (global plan-focused search, local tailored MCTS) that reshapes candidate expansion in web action spaces; lab results on WebArena and MiniWoB++.

KAIJU's claim is decoupling execution from reasoning via an executive kernel that plans upfront and schedules tools with dependency resolution; compared with a ReAct baseline in the lab (IGX gating is the runner-up).
Headline artefact is an instrumented bounded-memory testbed and reusable methodology (298 tagged trajectories) for isolating memory layers; evidence is a fixed-A0 ablation inside the harness.

AgentRadio contributes the inter-agent communication layer itself (threads, messages, waiting for mentions) under a division-of-labor protocol; measured on SWE-Atlas QnA against single-agent baselines.

Recuris is an outer loop in which a Meta-Agent turns execution evidence into validation-gated Skill Memory updates (recursive self-improvement); validated on four long-horizon benchmarks across ten models.
ACM gives the agent context-editing tools to decide when to compress, offload to external memory and retrieve on demand; lab evaluation on agentic search and coding after a post-training pipeline.

Contribution is a diagnostic methodology instrumenting tasks with checkpoints to locate where long-horizon agents fail; tested in the lab via a pre-specified 92-seed intervention study across two models.
Weighted Memory Tree decides which memories stay active via retention scores, decay and folding; lab evaluation on GAIA-Text with three models plus ablations and memory-poisoning tests.
Entropy-Guided Branching changes the shape of exploration by expanding branches where predictive entropy is high; evaluated in the lab on the SLATE benchmark the paper also releases.
HiAgent manages in-trial working memory by chunking history under subgoals and replacing old action-observation pairs with summaries; lab results across five long-horizon tasks.

CHILL-Harness decides which workflow adaptations are worth their cost, realizing only interventions with sufficient expected advantage; lab experiments show preserved success with lower token and time spend.

Faramesh is a non-bypassable pre-execution authorization boundary issuing PERMIT/DEFER/DENY that executors must validate; the paper argues the design and shows how the primitives work, with no measured study.

The artefact is SWE-Marathon itself, 20 ultra-long-horizon tasks with executable environments and multi-layer verification, used to measure frontier agents and characterize their failure modes in the lab.
InterruptBench is the instrument: a WebArena-Lite-derived benchmark plus interruption simulation framework, used in a lab study of six backbones under addition, revision and retraction interruptions.
ELHPlan contributes Action Chains as the planning primitive with a construct-validate-refine-execute cycle that avoids full replanning; validated in the lab on TDW-MAT and C-WAH.
MemAct treats working-memory curation as learnable in-place edit actions (deletion, insertion) optimized end-to-end; lab experiments report accuracy at 51% shorter average context.
